builder_plan.scenario: A multi-step product task fails because the agent loses track of dependencies.
builder_plan.change: Try the proposed planning step on tasks with checkable intermediate outcomes.
builder_plan.baseline: The same agent solving the same tasks without the new planning step.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task completion, unnecessary steps, planning tokens, response time, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
summary: ZeroVLN replaces navigation-domain supervised fine-tuning of a VLM with a semantic tool-calling interface in which the frozen VLM brain issues natural-language movement decisions that a small action expert executes, with both policies then jointly improved via closed-loop reinforcement learning. The cost is an RL training pipeline in the VLN-CE simulator, an additional action expert to train and maintain, and extra latency from the slow-fast loop; the claimed benefit is avoiding degradation of the VLM's general capabilities. It can fail if the natural-language interface miscommunicates geometry, if RL-trained policies do not transfer outside the simulated environments, or if the RL compute exceeds a constrained budget.
rationale: The paper targets vision-language navigation in simulators with closed-loop RL training, which is outside typical production LLM work and requires RL infrastructure and VLN-CE environments rather than being adoptable as an inference technique.
technique: Zero-SFT slow-fast VLN with tool-calling interface

claims.statement: ZeroVLN replaces navigation-domain supervised fine-tuning of a VLM with a semantic tool-calling interface in which the frozen VLM brain issues natural-language movement decisions that a small action expert executes, with both policies then jointly improved via closed-loop reinforcement learning. The cost is an RL training pipeline in the VLN-CE simulator, an additional action expert to train and maintain, and extra latency from the slow-fast loop; the claimed benefit is avoiding degradation of the VLM's general capabilities. It can fail if the natural-language interface miscommunicates geometry, if RL-trained policies do not transfer outside the simulated environments, or if the RL compute exceeds a constrained budget.

The abstract states ZeroVLN substantially outperforms representative SFT-based hierarchical VLN methods on VLN-CE benchmarks while largely preserving the base VLM's general capabilities, but provides no numerical results.
